angle: In Hamilton a hot tub or sauna is the reward at the end of a hard-working day: the steelworker coming down the Mountain at midnight, the nurse off a twelve-hour shift, the Dundas couple squeezing a soak into a side yard laid out a century ago, all of them wanting heat that holds through an escarpment winter.

hot-tub.intro: Hamilton tubs have to survive escarpment wind, lower-city side yards and shift-work schedules, so we stock everything from a plug-in Nordic to the J-500 series on our Ancaster floor, and every new 2026 Jacuzzi in stock is 20% off under the Red Tag clearance.
body: The escarpment splits Hamilton weather in two. The lower city, Stoney Creek and Grimsby sit in Lake Ontario's shelter and see more freezing rain than deep snow, while the Mountain, Ancaster, Binbrook and Waterdown run a few degrees colder and take the full sweep of the west wind across open ground. A tub on the brow or in a Binbrook subdivision needs a heavier cover with locking straps, a cabinet turned away from the wind and a path you will actually shovel in February. Down below, drainage matters more than snow load, because a spring thaw off the slope can leave a low pad sitting in water.

Housing here comes in two shapes. Older lower-city streets, Westdale, Dundas and the old part of Stoney Creek have deep narrow lots, a detached garage at the back and a side yard barely wider than a wheelbarrow, so we measure gates and eave heights before we quote and bring a crane when the tub has to go over the house. Subdivisions in Ancaster, Waterdown, Binbrook and upper Stoney Creek give us a fence gate and a flat yard, but the panel is often on the far wall of a finished basement, so the electrical run is where the budget moves. A licensed ESA electrician handles the circuit either way.

Who buys here is as varied as the streets. Hospital and McMaster staff on rotating shifts want a tub they can slip into at two in the morning without waking the house, so the quieter J-300 and J-400 series get a lot of attention. Steel and trades families lean toward seven-seat tubs like the J-345 at $23,195 or the Aquasolus The Calma at $13,995 that fit the whole crew after a long week. Retirees downsizing to a bungalow in Ancaster or Grimsby often choose a J-404L at $25,195, a lounger and a real jet count in a compact footprint. All of them are running on our floor.

faq.q: Does living on the Mountain change which tub I should buy?
faq.a: Not the model so much as the setup. The Mountain, Ancaster and Binbrook get more wind and a few more degrees of cold than the lower city, so we specify a heavier cover, a lifter that will not act like a sail and full-foam insulation, which every Jacuzzi has. If your yard faces open farmland to the west, a privacy screen or a fence panel on that side pays for itself in heating costs.

faq.q: My lower-city side yard is under a metre wide. Can you still deliver?
faq.a: Usually, yes, and we see this every week in Hamilton, Dundas and Westdale. Most tubs travel on edge on a dolly and need roughly 90 centimetres of clear width plus a straight run, so a gas meter, a downspout or an air conditioner in the gap is what actually stops us. When the gap is too tight or the garage blocks the yard, a crane over the house takes about an hour and we arrange it as part of the delivery.

faq.q: How does an escarpment slope affect where the tub goes?
faq.a: Water always wins on a slope, so the pad has to be level and drained, not just flat. On terraced Dundas and Mountain-brow lots we usually recommend a poured concrete pad set into the grade with a gravel apron, or a properly footed deck rather than patio stones that heave with the spring thaw. Keep the tub on the same terrace as the door you will use, because carrying wet towels up steps in January gets old fast.

faq.q: I work rotating shifts. Is a hot tub practical for odd hours in winter?
faq.a: It is one of the most common reasons Hamilton buyers give us. Jacuzzi tubs with the SmartTub system let you nudge the temperature from the parking lot so the water is ready when you pull in, and a 240V tub holds its set point around the clock so there is no waiting. Position it near a door with a motion light and keep a hook for the cover straps so a three in the morning soak takes thirty seconds to open.

faq.q: When is the best time of year to take delivery in Hamilton?
faq.a: October and November are the sweet spot: the ground is firm for the pad, the crews are not fighting snowbanks in a side yard and you are in the water for the first cold snap. Spring deliveries work well on the Mountain and in Binbrook where lots are flat, but lower-city and Dundas yards can stay soft into May. Winter delivery is fine as long as the path is cleared and the electrician can get in.

swim-spa.intro: Swim spas suit Hamilton lots that were never going to fit a pool: a lower-city yard hemmed in by a garage, a Binbrook or Waterdown subdivision lot with a short rear setback, or an escarpment terrace with one flat spot.
body: A swim spa in Hamilton is a lap pool for people who train year-round: triathletes who ride the rail trail all summer and need somewhere to swim in February, McMaster athletes and staff, physiotherapy patients sent home with aquatic exercises, and parents who want the kids in the water without a full pool to close every fall. The current adjusts from a gentle walk to a hard swim, and the water holds its temperature through the coldest week of January because the shell is fully insulated and covered, which no backyard pool in this climate can claim.

Delivery is the first conversation. A 14 foot J-14 PowerActive weighs enough that it always comes in by crane, so we look at the street, the hydro lines and the distance over the house before we quote. Older streets below the Mountain often have overhead lines and mature maples, and Dundas has narrow streets on the valley floor, so the crane may need a lane closure and we handle that paperwork. New builds in Binbrook, upper Stoney Creek and Waterdown are usually a straightforward lift over the rear fence from the road behind or from a neighbouring lot with permission.

Which model depends on how you will use it. Serious swimmers pick the 16 or 19 foot PowerPro models, with the J-16 PowerPro at $54,295 the most popular because it fits a standard suburban lot with room left for a patio. Families choose the 13 foot J-13 PowerPlay at $33,195 with eight seats, or the 12 foot J-12 Flow at $30,695 that fits where a two-car parking pad would. A household that wants a real hot tub as well takes a dual-temperature model like the J-19DT PowerActive at $53,295, so one end runs hot while the swim lane stays cool.

faq.q: Will a swim spa fit on a new subdivision lot in Binbrook or Stoney Creek?
faq.a: Most of the time. A 14 foot model needs a footprint about the size of a single parking space plus a walkway, and rear yards in the newer Glanbrook and upper Stoney Creek subdivisions typically give you that, though the setback from the rear and side fences is set by the City of Hamilton, so check before you pour. A 12 or 13 foot J-12 Flow or J-13 PowerPlay is the safe pick when the lot is on the smaller side.

faq.q: Do I have to drain a swim spa for winter?
faq.a: No. A swim spa is built to run all winter with the heater on and the cover closed, and draining one in a Hamilton December is the fastest way to crack a pump. Owners typically drain and refill in spring and fall when the weather is mild, and we can schedule a service visit to time the changeover with your water test.

faq.q: How does wind on the escarpment brow affect a swim spa?
faq.a: Wind strips heat off any open water, and the brow from Ancaster through the Mountain to Stoney Creek gets a steady westerly. A swim spa is covered when not in use so the standing loss is small, but during a swim the exposed surface is large. A fence, a hedge or the house itself on the west side cuts the draft and keeps the water comfortable for a longer session.

faq.q: Which swim spa suits a family that wants swimming and soaking in one unit?
faq.a: The dual-temperature models. The J-19DT PowerPro at $60,895 and J-19DT PowerActive at $53,295 have a swim end and a hot tub end on separate heaters, and the SwimLife SwimExpert DualStream 19 at $56,095 pairs a 19 foot lane with an attached five-person hot tub. They are the longest units we sell, so they suit the bigger Ancaster and Flamborough lots better than a lower-city yard.

faq.q: Does a swim spa need a pool fence or permit around Hamilton?
faq.a: Rules vary by municipality and Hamilton, Haldimand County, Brantford and Grimsby each treat spas a little differently, so ask the building department before you dig. A lockable safety cover satisfies the enclosure rule in many cases, but a sunken or plumbed-in unit can trigger a pool enclosure permit. We supply the dimensions and drawings you need for the application.

sauna.intro: Long lower-city winters, Mountain wind and shift-work recovery make Hamilton a natural sauna market, and the two routes are simple: a Clearlight infrared cabin in the basement of a century home, or a Serenity cedar sauna on a Flamborough or Ancaster lot.
body: Older Hamilton homes were built before anyone imagined a sauna in the basement, so ceiling height and the width of the stairs decide the cabin. Clearlight Sanctuary cabins arrive in flat panels and go together in a couple of hours, and the Sanctuary 1 at $10,495 and Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 fit under the low joists common in North End and Westdale semis. They plug into a standard outlet, which matters in a house with a 100 amp panel already carrying a dryer and an air conditioner. Newer builds in Waterdown or Binbrook with nine foot basements can take the four-person Sanctuary Y at $13,995.

Outdoor cedar saunas belong on the rural and estate lots: Flamborough, the Ancaster side roads, Mount Hope, the farm properties around Caledonia and the bench above Grimsby. A Serenity Sauna at $17,495 or the smaller Serenity Mini at $14,995 sits on a gravel pad or deck footings, the heater is chosen separately, and a wood-burning option suits properties where running a new 240V circuit out to the back of the lot would cost more than the sauna. Western red cedar weathers grey on the windward side over a few winters, and most owners like it that way.

The buyers we see most are people whose bodies take a beating: nurses and paramedics coming off nights, ironworkers and millwrights, hockey parents who spent the weekend in a cold arena, and McMaster staff who read about heat therapy and want to try it before they buy. Both cabin types are set up on our Ancaster floor and running, so you can sit in each for ten minutes and feel the difference between infrared warmth and a hot cedar room before deciding which one goes home.

faq.q: Will an infrared cabin fit in the basement of a century home in the lower city?
faq.a: Usually. The one and two person Sanctuary cabins are built for low ceilings and tight stairs, and the panels come in through a standard door. Measure the lowest beam or duct on the path and tell us, and we will confirm the fit before it ships. A dehumidifier in the room helps in an old fieldstone basement.

faq.q: Can an outdoor Serenity sauna sit on a sloped Dundas or escarpment lot?
faq.a: Yes, on a level platform. We recommend a small deck on adjustable footings or a poured pad cut into the grade rather than trying to level a slope with gravel alone, because frost heave on the escarpment will move anything that is not footed. Put the door on the uphill side so meltwater runs away from the threshold.

faq.q: How do people here pair a sauna with a cold plunge?
faq.a: The routine is heat, cold, rest, repeated two or three times, and it is popular with shift workers and athletes recovering after a night or a game. The Sanctuary 2, 3 and Y pair naturally with a Chill Tubs Essential, and we can deliver and set up both together. Most owners put the plunge just outside the sauna door so the walk between the two is a few steps in bare feet, even in January.

faq.q: Does the cedar need finishing for Hamilton weather?
faq.a: Leave the inside bare, always, because finishes off-gas in a hot room. On the outside you can let the Western red cedar weather naturally or apply a clear penetrating oil every couple of years to hold the colour. On the Mountain and in Flamborough the windward wall greys faster, so some owners oil that side alone.

faq.q: How long does an infrared sauna take to warm up in an unheated garage?
faq.a: Longer than in a basement. Infrared heats your body more than the air, so you can step in after ten or fifteen minutes even when the cabin has not reached its set point, but a garage that sits near freezing in January slows things considerably. Most Hamilton owners put the cabin in a basement, a spare room or a corner of a detached garage that has some heat.

hot-tub.small: Small tubs solve two Hamilton problems: a lower-city yard where a full-size shell will not clear the garage, and a semi-rural property in Flamborough or Mount Hope where the panel is already tapped out. The Nordic Sport All-In-110V at $7,295 and Nordic Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 plug into a standard outlet and ride a dolly through a narrow gate, while the Jacuzzi J-315 at $18,795 gives a couple three seats and 23 jets in a footprint that fits a Westdale side patio. The J-404L at $25,195 is the compact tub with a proper lounger for downsizers in Ancaster and Grimsby.
hot-tub.medium: Five and six seat tubs are the sweet spot for family homes in Stoney Creek, Waterdown and on the Mountain, where a couple plus two kids plus the occasional neighbour is the normal load. The J-335 at $21,995 is the best-selling size in our Ancaster showroom, the J-235 at $16,295 keeps the budget in check, and the J-445 at $27,895 adds the J-400 series lighting and waterfall for a yard you look at from the kitchen. The Wellness Shop Ontario L S103 at $15,595 offers six seats and 51 jets for a trades family that wants pressure over polish.
hot-tub.large: Seven seats and up is for the Hamilton family that hosts: steel and trades households with adult kids still around, hockey teams after a Sunday tournament, the Binbrook new build with an oversized lot and a walkout. The J-509 at $39,595 with eight seats and 76 jets is the flagship, the J-495 at $34,595 seats nine, and the J-385 at $26,595 and J-285 at $18,695 give seven seats at friendlier prices. On the value end, the Aquasolus The Cove at $11,995 seats seven and includes White Glove delivery, which covers a lot of the crane and side yard headaches on older lots.

productNotes.swim-spa: Swim spas replace the pool that never fit. On lower-city and Dundas lots they go in by crane over the house, and on Binbrook, Waterdown and Stoney Creek subdivision lots they usually lift over the rear fence. Serious swimmers pick the PowerPro line, families take the J-13 PowerPlay at $33,195 or the J-12 Flow at $30,695, and the SwimLife SwimFit SwimStream 14 at $38,095 is the value pick for someone who just wants to swim against a current in February without heating a full pool.
productNotes.sauna: Clearlight infrared cabins from $10,495 fit the basements and spare rooms of older Hamilton homes, plug into a standard outlet and heat quickly for daily recovery after a shift. Serenity cedar saunas from $14,995 belong outdoors on Flamborough, Ancaster and Caledonia properties with room for a gravel pad and a heater of your choice. Both are set up and running on the Ancaster floor so you can feel the difference between a gentle infrared session and a proper hot cedar room before you decide.
productNotes.cold-plunge: Cold plunges have caught on with Hamilton's shift workers, paramedics and athletes as the second half of a heat and cold routine. The Chill Tubs range, from the Essential Bath and Pod through the Obsidian and the Pro, chills and filters its own water so you are not filling a stock tank with bags of ice. They run on a standard outlet, fit on a patio or in a garage, and pair with a Clearlight or Serenity sauna. Pricing is set in the showroom, and we can quote a Chill Tub together with any Sanctuary cabin.

financing: A hot tub in Hamilton is often bought around a work schedule rather than a season: a steel or trades household paid every two weeks, a nurse whose overtime lands in one lump, a Binbrook family that just closed on a new build and would rather keep cash for the fence and the deck. Bi-weekly payments line up with that, with Nordic tubs from $15.01 bi-weekly and 0% for 12 months on approved credit across the range. Bring your quote to the Ancaster showroom and we will run the numbers on a couple of terms while you sit in the tub.
showroom: The Wellness Shop at Jacuzzi Hamilton is at 1015 Golf Links Road in Ancaster, in the Meadowlands just off Highway 403, with free parking at the door. The floor has Jacuzzi J-200 through J-500 tubs filled and running, Nordic and Aquasolus tubs beside them, a swim spa you can climb into, and a Clearlight infrared cabin and a Serenity cedar sauna both heated so you can step inside. Bring a swimsuit and a towel and book a wet test, or just walk in and sit on the edges.

Ancaster is the hinge of the region, which is why one showroom works for so many towns. Dundas and Westdale are ten minutes down the hill, the Mountain is a straight run along the LINC, Binbrook and Stoney Creek come across on the LINC and the Red Hill, Brantford is half an hour west on the 403 and Grimsby comes up the QEW. Most customers visit twice: once to shortlist, once with the family to decide.

Ancaster.lead: Ancaster is home turf: the showroom sits in the Meadowlands and many of our installs are within a few kilometres, on everything from village lots along Wilson Street to estate properties on the side roads.
body: Ancaster housing splits between the old village core and the subdivisions that grew around the Meadowlands and out toward the Sulphur Springs side roads. Village lots have mature trees and older detached garages, so we scout the side yard before quoting and occasionally bring a crane. The newer streets have flat rear yards and a gate wide enough for a dolly, and the panel is usually in the basement close to the back wall. Estate lots on the west side often have room for a Serenity cedar sauna beside the tub and a longer electrical run.

Buyers here are established: hospital physicians and administrators, McMaster faculty, retirees who traded a Toronto house for a bungalow near the golf course, and families who host. The J-400 series is the volume seller, with the J-445 at $27,895 and J-485 at $30,795 the usual shortlist, and the eight-seat J-509 at $39,595 goes to the larger properties. Ancaster sits on top of the escarpment, so plan for wind and a bit more snow than Dundas below.
Ancaster.drive: You are already here. The showroom is at 1015 Golf Links Road in the Meadowlands, off Highway 403 at the Golf Links exit, with parking at the door.

Dundas.lead: Dundas sits in the valley below the escarpment with narrow Victorian lots, stone walls and side yards that were laid out for a horse, not a hot tub, which is exactly the kind of delivery our crews do well.
body: Most Dundas homes are older: red brick semis and detached houses on King Street and the streets that climb toward the Peak, with a detached garage at the back and a side path under a metre wide. We measure before we quote and plan the route to the centimetre, and when the gap is too tight a crane over the roof from the street is routine. Lots on the valley slopes need a level, drained pad because meltwater off the escarpment comes through in March. Compact tubs like the J-335 at $21,995 or the four-seat Aquasolus The Brook at $10,995 with White Glove delivery included fit these yards well.

Dundas buyers are often McMaster and hospital staff who bike or drive the short hop to campus, plus long-time residents who want a soak after gardening a steep lot. The town is sheltered from the wind by the escarpment on three sides but sits lower and damper, so a well-fitted cover and a spot that catches winter sun matter. Infrared cabins are popular in the low basements of the older houses, and the Clearlight Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 paired with a Chill Tubs Essential is a common setup.
Dundas.drive: Take Osler Drive or York Road up to Highway 403, head toward Ancaster and get off at Golf Links Road. About ten minutes from the valley floor.

Stoney Creek.lead: Stoney Creek runs from the lakeshore and the old town up the escarpment to the newer subdivisions on the Mountain, and the two halves have very different backyards and weather.
body: Old Stoney Creek and the lakeshore streets near Winona and Fruitland have mature lots with detached garages and side yards that call for a careful dolly route or a lift over the house. Upper Stoney Creek off Rymal Road and Highland Road is nearly all new build: narrow lots with a rear fence, a gate and a walkout, so delivery is simple but the rear setback is tight and a six-seat tub like the J-355 at $24,795 fits better than a nine-seater. Lake Ontario keeps the lower half milder, while the upper half takes the wind that sweeps across the Mountain.

Buyers are young families commuting on the Red Hill and the QEW, steelworkers and port workers on rotating shifts who live close to the plant, and retirees along the lake. Shift workers ask for tubs that stay quiet and ready at odd hours, and the J-300 series with the ProClear system does that. Along the lake the wind is the concern, so we turn the equipment door away from the water and add a cover lifter that locks down.
Stoney Creek.drive: Take the QEW or the Red Hill Valley Parkway to the LINC, follow it west across the Mountain to Highway 403, then exit at Golf Links Road. Allow about 25 minutes.

Waterdown.lead: Waterdown sits on top of the escarpment north of the city, mostly newer subdivisions around an old village core, with the wind and snow that come with elevation and open farmland to the north.
body: Nearly every Waterdown backyard we deliver to is a subdivision lot from the last twenty years: a rear fence, a side gate, a walkout or a deck off the kitchen, and a panel in a basement that is often already finished. Access is easy and the question is where the tub sits relative to the deck and how far the electrician has to run conduit. Homes in the old village near Mill Street and Dundas Street have deeper lots with mature trees and the occasional stone foundation, so we scout those before quoting.

Waterdown families commute to Burlington, Oakville and Toronto on the 403 and 407 or from Aldershot GO, so the tub gets used late in the evening in a yard that catches the north wind. Six and seven seat tubs sell best: the J-365 at $24,795 and J-345 at $23,195 for growing families, the J-408 at $29,995 for the larger corner lots. A Clearlight Sanctuary 3 at $12,995 in the finished basement is a common second purchase once the tub has proven itself.
Waterdown.drive: Take Highway 6 south to Highway 403, head toward Hamilton and exit at Golf Links Road in Ancaster. About 15 minutes without traffic, or come across Highway 5 and down through Dundas.

Binbrook.lead: Binbrook is Hamilton's newest corner, a former farm village on Highway 56 surrounded by subdivisions where nearly every lot is a fresh rectangle waiting for a deck and a tub.
body: The subdivisions off Binbrook Road and Highway 56 are new build almost to a house: rear fences, standard side gates, sod that is still settling and a basement panel with room for a 50 amp breaker. Delivery is quick but the ground is the issue, because Glanbrook sits on heavy clay that heaves in spring, so we insist on a compacted gravel base or a poured pad rather than patio stones on sand. Lots here are flat and open, and the west wind off the fields is constant in winter, so fence placement matters for heating costs.

Binbrook buyers are young families who bought their first detached house here, often with two incomes, a couple of kids and a trades van in the driveway. Seven-seat tubs at family prices sell well: the J-245 at $16,295, the Wellness Shop Ontario S104 at $15,595 with two 6 HP pumps for a household of hockey players, and the J-385 at $26,595 when the budget allows. Water is municipal in the subdivisions, but some older village and concession properties are on wells, which changes the start-up chemistry.
Binbrook.drive: Take Highway 56 north to Rymal Road, then follow Rymal west across the Mountain until it becomes Garner Road in Ancaster and turn onto Golf Links Road. Plan on 25 minutes.

Caledonia.lead: Caledonia is a Grand River town in Haldimand County, twenty minutes south on Highway 6, with an old main street of brick homes, new subdivisions on the edges and farm properties in every direction.
body: In the older part of town along Argyle Street and the river, lots are deep and narrow with detached garages, so delivery is a dolly down the side or a crane over the house, much like the lower city. The subdivisions on the north and east edges are standard new-build yards with fence gates and flat grades. Outside town, farm and country properties give us room to work, but the panel is often in a barn or a detached shop, so the electrical run is the number we settle first. Rural lots are usually on wells, which shifts the water care toward hardness and metals.

Caledonia buyers are farmers, trades families, nurses and firefighters commuting up Highway 6 to Hamilton, and people who moved down from the city for a bigger lot. Country properties suit a Serenity Sauna at $17,495 with a wood-burning heater, no new circuit required, beside a J-345 at $23,195 or a Wellness Shop Ontario S106 at $17,695. Haldimand County sets its own setbacks and permit rules, so call the county before pouring the pad.
Caledonia.drive: Take Highway 6 north past the airport to Highway 403, then head toward Hamilton one exit to Golf Links Road. The trip runs about 25 minutes.

Brantford.lead: Brantford is a 403 city on the Grand River, half an hour west, with century homes near the downtown and the Laurier campus, post-war streets and fast-growing West Brant subdivisions.
body: Brantford's older neighbourhoods, Eagle Place, Holmedale and the streets around the downtown, have generous lots by Hamilton standards but the same detached garages and side paths, so the crane question still comes up. West Brant and the north end near Powerline Road are almost entirely new build with flat rear yards and easy gate access. Brantford draws its water from the Grand River and it behaves differently from Hamilton's lake water, so we set up water care for it, and rural lots toward Paris and Mount Pleasant are often on wells.

Brantford buyers are a mix of long-time trades and manufacturing families, parents who bought a house for a Laurier student instead of paying rent, commuters heading east on the 403 to Hamilton and Mississauga, and retirees on the golf course streets. Value sells: the J-275 floor clearance from $14,695, the Aquasolus The Calma at $13,995 with White Glove delivery, and the Nordic Retreat SE at $10,195 for a smaller yard. The Wayne Gretzky Parkway side of the city has the newest lots and the most swim spa interest.
Brantford.drive: Take Highway 403 east for about 30 minutes and exit at Golf Links Road in Ancaster; the showroom is a minute off the ramp in the Meadowlands, before you reach Hamilton traffic.

Grimsby.lead: Grimsby is squeezed between Lake Ontario and the escarpment at the start of Niagara wine country, a QEW commuter town with lakeside condos, old town lots and bench properties above the ridge.
body: Lakeside Grimsby, the newer streets near Casablanca Boulevard and the old town below the escarpment have the mildest winters in our territory thanks to the lake, but the wind off the water in January is relentless and freezing rain is more common than snow. Lots range from narrow old-town yards with detached garages to condo terraces where a compact Nordic Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 on a plug is the only tub that fits. Up on the bench, properties are larger, sometimes on wells, and a Serenity cedar sauna beside the tub is a natural fit.

Grimsby buyers are Toronto and Hamilton commuters who ride the QEW or the GO bus, wine and hospitality people who work weekends and soak on Mondays, and retirees who moved for the microclimate. Six-seat tubs with a lounger like the J-375 at $25,295 and J-508L at $35,695 suit couples who entertain, and the two-person Clearlight Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 is popular with the wellness crowd. Grimsby sits in Niagara Region, so permit and setback questions go to the town, not Hamilton.
Grimsby.drive: Take the QEW toward Hamilton, climb the escarpment on the Red Hill Valley Parkway, then take the LINC west to Highway 403 and Golf Links Road. Roughly 35 minutes.

Mount Hope.lead: Mount Hope is the airport village on Highway 6 south of the Mountain, a mix of older village homes, hobby farms and rural lots where a hot tub competes with the tractor for the panel.
body: Most Mount Hope properties are rural or semi-rural: a house set back from the road, a detached shop or barn, a long gravel drive and plenty of room to park a delivery truck. Access is rarely the problem. The electrical is, because the panel may be in the shop rather than the house and the run to a good tub spot can be long, so we settle that with the electrician before quoting. Wells are common, so we start with a water test and set the chemistry for hardness and iron. Aircraft noise is part of life here, and a tub in the lee of the house is quieter.

Buyers are airport and cargo workers on shift rotations, farmers, contractors who run a business from the shop, and Hamilton families who moved out for space. A Nordic Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 is the quick answer when the panel is full, and the Serenity Sauna at $17,495 with a wood-burning heater suits a lot with a woodpile. Families with room take the J-485 at $30,795 or the Ontario S106 at $17,695 with its two 6 HP pumps.
Mount Hope.drive: Head north on Highway 6 to Highway 403 and go toward Hamilton one exit to Golf Links Road, or take Upper James to Rymal Road and Garner Road west into the Meadowlands. Under 15 minutes.

Flamborough.lead: Flamborough is Hamilton's rural north: Carlisle, Freelton, Millgrove, Greensville and Rockton, with country lots, horse properties and older village homes strung along Highways 5, 6 and 8.
body: Flamborough deliveries are about distance, not width. Long driveways, rear yards a hundred metres from the road and a panel in a house that predates air conditioning are the normal conditions, so we walk the route with you and the electrician together. Greensville and the streets above Dundas sit on the escarpment with slope and drainage to manage, while Carlisle and Freelton are flat and open to the wind. Almost every property outside the villages is on a well, so we test the water first and set up the tub accordingly.

Flamborough buyers are horse people, farmers, contractors and Hamilton and Burlington commuters who wanted acreage and now want a reward at the end of the day. Outdoor cedar saunas sell better here than anywhere else in our territory, with the Serenity Sauna at $17,495 next to a seven-seat J-365 at $24,795 or J-485 at $30,795 the common set. Wood-burning heaters suit properties with a woodlot. Snow load on covers is real here, and we recommend clearing the cover after any storm that drops more than fifteen centimetres.
Flamborough.drive: From Carlisle or Freelton take Highway 6 south to Highway 403 and exit at Golf Links Road; from Greensville or Rockton come down Highway 8 or Highway 52. Twenty to thirty minutes.

productBlurbs.j-509: Flagship of the floor and the tub for the Ancaster household that hosts: eight open seats mean a full table of adult kids and their partners fit without anyone perched on the edge, and 76 jets are spread across every station so the last person in still gets a real massage. ProClarity 6-Stage filtration keeps up with that kind of crowd. Under the Red Tag clearance the J-509 sits at $39,595, and it is filled and running in the Meadowlands.
productBlurbs.j-508: Seven open seats with no lounger eating the footprint make the J-508 the sensible J-500 for a Waterdown family that wants everyone in at once after a long 403 commute. The J-509 adds one more seat and 20 more jets, but most households never fill it, and the 56 jets here are placed so the corner seats are as good as the middle ones. Priced at $35,695 with six-stage filtration that lets you skip a weekend of water fiddling.
productBlurbs.j-508l: If you would rather have more pressure per person than another seat, this is the J-500 to sit in first. Six open seats share 60 jets, so each station gets more coverage than the seven-seat J-508 at the same $35,695 price, and the True Water system with ProClarity 6-Stage filtration handles a lakeshore lot in Stoney Creek where a westerly keeps blowing leaves into the yard. Couples who entertain a few times a month tell us it is the right compromise.
productBlurbs.j-408: Hockey families in the Glanbrook subdivisions ask for a tub that holds two adults and a carload of kids after a Sunday tournament, and the J-408 is the J-400 model we point them to. Seven open seats and 41 jets on a wide shell, ProClarity 5-Stage filtration to cope with a lot of bodies, and the J-400 lighting package that makes the yard worth looking at from a walkout kitchen. Its Red Tag price is $29,995, applied at the counter.
productBlurbs.j-408l: A nurse coming off nights at Juravinski wants a lounger she can lie flat in and five other seats for when the household joins later, which is exactly the J-408L layout. Same $29,995 Red Tag price as the open-seating J-408, one fewer seat, and 39 jets concentrated where a tired back and calves want them. On a Mountain brow lot we pair it with the heavier cover and a lifter that locks, because the wind up there does not take a night off.
productBlurbs.j-404l: Four seats, one of them a full lounger, in a footprint that fits the side patio of a Westdale semi without swallowing it. The J-404L is the compact J-400 for two people who soak most nights and have company occasionally, and its 32 jets are not spread thin. You keep the J-400 series cabinet, waterfall and ProClarity 5-Stage filtration in a shell a dolly can wheel past a downspout. Red Tag pricing brings it to $25,195.
productBlurbs.j-495: Nine seats is the answer for a Caledonia farm property where the whole crew, hired hands included, ends up in the tub after harvest. The J-495 is the widest shell in the J-400 line with 71 jets spread across every station, and the 2025 floor model in our showroom is tagged at $31,395 as a clearance unit. That one has been running on our floor for months, so you can see exactly how the seating works before it goes on the truck.
productBlurbs.j-485: Seven open seats and 49 jets on a shell that handles the wind off the fields around Mount Hope, where a tub sits in the open more often than not. The J-485 is a step up from the J-445 in seats and jet count for a family with teenagers who each want their own spot. Ask about the 2025 floor model, marked down to $26,295, before you look at the new stock; it carries the full Jacuzzi warranty just the same.
productBlurbs.j-475: Hospitality people on the Grimsby bench who work weekends and soak on a Monday afternoon tend to want a lounger and a crowd option in one tub. The J-475 gives seven seats with a lounger and 55 jets, the most in the J-400 range short of the nine-seat J-495, and the lounger is long enough that a six-foot server does not float out of it. A 2025 floor model is priced at $26,295, and new 2026 units qualify for the Red Tag 20%.
productBlurbs.j-445: On a Kirkendall lot where the tub comes over the house by crane, a six-seat open shell like the J-445 is the largest most crews will lift comfortably, and it leaves room for a chair beside it. Six open seats mean nobody argues over a lounger, and 45 jets cover the bench seats well. Our 2025 floor model is $23,995 in clearance, or take a new 2026 unit under the Red Tag and choose your cabinet colour.
productBlurbs.j-435: Paramedics in the upper Stoney Creek subdivisions off Rymal Road describe the ideal tub as a lounger for the one who just finished a shift plus room for the rest of the family, and the J-435 is that tub. Six seats with a lounger and 47 jets, two more than the open-seat J-445, on a J-400 shell with ProClarity 5-Stage filtration. Our 2025 floor unit is $24,995, and it has been running on the floor since spring.
productBlurbs.j-385: Top of the J-300 range, and the seven-seat tub we sell most to Mountain households near Mohawk College where two working adults and three kids all want in on a Friday. Seven open seats and 51 jets, plus the CLEARRAY Active Oxygen water care and the ProClear skimming weir that pulls leaves and grit off the surface before they sink. Under the Red Tag it lists at $26,595, which puts J-400 seating within reach of a J-300 budget.
productBlurbs.j-365: Seven seats for the price of many six-seaters is the J-365 argument, and it lands well with commuters who come home late off the GO train and want a tub that holds temperature all evening for whoever gets in last. Its 46 jets are placed for the corner seats as much as the centre, the CLEARRAY Active Oxygen system keeps chemical use down, and the shell fits a standard subdivision rear yard with a walkway around it. Red Tag pricing: $24,795.
productBlurbs.j-345: Seven seats at a price a North End family near the Bayfront can carry on a single income is why the J-345 moves so steadily off our floor. You give up ten jets against the J-385 and keep everything that matters: the open layout, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen water care, the ProClear weir and the full-foam shell that shrugs off a lakeside January. Red Tag pricing brings it to $23,195, with delivery to the lower city handled by crews who know the alleys.
productBlurbs.j-375: For someone who spends Saturdays working a steep Dundas garden and wants the lounger to themselves that evening, the J-375 is the J-300 to try first. Six seats including a full lounger, and 52 jets, the highest count in the J-300 line, aimed at lower back, hips and feet. The ProClear system with its ProCatch bag makes sense on a valley lot where maple keys and blossom land in the water all spring. Red Tag price: $25,295.
productBlurbs.j-355: A dock worker off a twelve-hour shift at the harbour wants a lounger, not a conversation, and the J-355 puts one in a six-seat shell that still holds the family on a Sunday. Its 44 jets sit between the J-335 and the J-375 in count, and the True Water system with CLEARRAY Active Oxygen means the water is ready without a nightly chemistry session. On the Red Tag it is $24,795, and it is filled on the floor in the Meadowlands.
productBlurbs.j-335: Our most-shortlisted six-seater, and the tub that goes to West Brant subdivisions in Brantford more than any other. The J-335 pairs a lounger with five open seats and 42 jets in a shell that lifts cleanly over a rear fence on a new-build lot, and the J-300 cabinet and lighting look right beside a composite deck. Grand River water behaves differently from lake water, so we set the CLEARRAY Active Oxygen start-up for it. Red Tag: $21,995.
productBlurbs.j-325: Five open seats with a modest 23 jets suits a Greensville couple who soak for the heat more than the massage and want room when the grandchildren visit. The J-325 runs the same CLEARRAY Active Oxygen water care and ProClear filtration as the bigger J-300 tubs, in a shell that sits on a small deck cut into an escarpment grade without a lift. Under the Red Tag it is $20,495, the lowest way into the J-300 series with five seats.
productBlurbs.j-315: Three seats and a lounger in a shell narrow enough for a Durand townhouse courtyard, which is where a lot of J-315s end up in Hamilton. It is a couple's tub with a third seat for a guest, 23 jets concentrated rather than spread, and the full J-300 water care so a small tub does not mean more maintenance. The compact shell also rides a dolly through gaps a five-seater cannot. Red Tag pricing puts it at $18,795.
productBlurbs.j-285: Seven open seats and 42 jets is a lot of tub for $18,695, and that is why the J-285 goes home with so many first-time buyers in Binbrook who just closed on a detached house. It is the top of the J-200 line, with CLEARRAY UV-C water care and a ProClassic 2-Stage filter that is simple to service, on a shell built for a flat new-build yard where the ground is the only thing to sort out. Every new 2026 unit carries the Red Tag 20%.
productBlurbs.j-245: Red Hill commuters with young kids who want seven seats without a J-300 budget end up between the J-245 and the J-285, and the difference is five jets and one price step. The J-245 keeps the open layout, CLEARRAY UV-C sanitation and the ProClassic filter with its ProCatch bag, and the shell clears a standard side gate on a dolly. At $16,295 under the Red Tag it is the least expensive seven-seat Jacuzzi on our floor.
productBlurbs.j-275: A floor clearance nobody expects: a 2025 J-275 with a lounger, six seats and 38 jets from $14,695, which is J-200 pricing on a tub with a proper lounge layout. It suits a Caledonia trades family that wants the lounger for one tired back and five seats for everyone else, and the CLEARRAY UV-C system keeps water care simple on a well. Stock is limited to what is on the floor, so ask which unit is here.
productBlurbs.j-235: Steelworkers on rotating shifts tell us they want a lounger, a tub that is ready at two in the morning and a price that does not need a second conversation at home, which describes the J-235. Six seats with a lounger and 34 jets, CLEARRAY UV-C water care and the ProClassic 2-Stage filter, all on a shell that holds heat through a lower-city sleet storm. The same $16,295 buys the open-seat J-245 with an extra seat if you host more than you lounge.
productBlurbs.j-225: Five open seats and 26 jets in a shell sized for a Waterdown townhome yard, where the rear fence is close and the deck takes half the space. The J-225 is the Jacuzzi for people who were looking at a Nordic and decided they wanted the CLEARRAY UV-C system and the Jacuzzi warranty behind it. At $14,695 under the Red Tag it costs the same as the six-seat J-275 clearance unit, so decide whether you want the extra seat or a brand new 2026 shell.
productBlurbs.j-215: Smallest Jacuzzi on the floor, and the one physiotherapy patients sent home with hydrotherapy exercises often choose: three seats, a lounger and 21 jets aimed at the joints that need them, in a shell light enough to place on an existing deck. The J-215 runs CLEARRAY UV-C water care and the ProClassic filter, and the compact footprint means a short electrical run in a lower-city semi. Red Tag pricing takes it to $14,095.
productBlurbs.retreat-all-in-110v: Plug it into a standard outlet and it runs, which is the entire reason the Retreat All-In-110V sells so well on Rockton and Carlisle properties where the electrical panel lives in a barn a long way from the patio. Five open seats, 13 jets and Nordic Clean ozone in a round shell built in Michigan, priced at $9,195 with the GFCI cord in the box. It is also the tub we can deliver fastest, because there is no electrician to schedule.
productBlurbs.sport-all-in-110v: Our least expensive hot tub, and the one that goes into Winona lakeside yards where the owner wants a soak this month, not after an electrician and an ESA inspection. The Sport All-In-110V has five seats, 15 jets, two more than the Retreat All-In-110V, and Nordic Clean ozone, on a 110V 15A cord. At $7,295 it is priced under what many people budget for a used tub, and it comes with a warranty and a delivery crew.
productBlurbs.retreat-se: When the side path of a Dundas semi is barely a wheelbarrow wide, a round Nordic goes where a square shell cannot, and the Retreat SE is the round tub with real jets. Five open seats and 29 jets on a 220V 40A circuit, roughly double the pressure of the plug-in Retreat All-In-110V, with Nordic Pure ozone keeping the water clear between changes. At $10,195 it is a hardwired Michigan-built tub for less than most entry-level rectangles.
productBlurbs.ontario-s106: Two 6 HP pumps behind 59 jets is the reason a Brantford manufacturing family who wants pressure picks the Ontario S106 over a similarly priced Jacuzzi J-200. Seven open seats, ozone filtration and Thermal Shield insulation on a USA-built shell, at $17,695. It is our own label, so we set the spec for Ontario winters rather than a mild climate, and it is filled beside the Jacuzzis on our floor so you can feel the jet difference for yourself.
productBlurbs.ontario-s104: Fifty-four jets and seven seats for $15,595 is the value pitch, and it lands with Freelton families on acreage who want a big tub for a crowd without paying for a premium badge. The Ontario S104 runs the same two 6 HP pumps as the S106 with five fewer jets, and Thermal Shield insulation keeps the hydro bill sane on an open lot where the wind never stops. Flow-through filtration and ozone keep the weekly routine short.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s103: A landscaper who is on his feet from April to November wants a lounger with pressure, not a gentle bubble, and the Ontario L S103 puts 51 jets behind two 6 HP pumps with a lounger in a six-seat layout. It costs the same $15,595 as the seven-seat S104, so the choice is a lounger versus a seventh seat. Thermal Shield insulation and a flow-through filter keep running costs and maintenance low for a household that would rather be in the tub than servicing it.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s105: An upgraded Ontario lounger: 56 jets, two 6 HP pumps and a GECKO K1000 keypad that is easy to read at night without your glasses. The L S105 is for the east-end commuter who gets in at eleven after the QEW and wants the lounger to do serious work on a stiff neck, with five more seats for the weekend. Priced at $17,695 with Thermal Shield insulation, and the keypad alone is worth comparing against the S103 on our floor.
productBlurbs.the-brook: Four seats and 23 jets from a European builder, with White Glove delivery and setup included, for $10,995: The Brook is the full-size tub for a Grimsby old-town yard where a crane over the garage was going to eat the savings on a cheaper unit. Superior Wellness builds it with an ozone system, and the smaller shell suits a couple who want a quality tub without a Jacuzzi price. It sits beside The Cove on our floor if you want to compare seat counts.
productBlurbs.the-cove: Seven seats for $11,995 including White Glove delivery is the sharpest number on our floor, and it belongs to The Cove. Superior Wellness builds it in Europe with an ozone system and 27 jets, so the pressure is gentler than a Jacuzzi J-245, but for a Mountain family that fills the tub after Sunday dinner and cares more about seats than massage, it is the obvious choice. Delivery and setup are already in the price.
productBlurbs.the-calma: Ten more jets than The Cove and the NaturaBalance shell make The Calma the Aquasolus we suggest to a Binbrook household that wants real massage in all seven seats without moving up to a Jacuzzi. Superior Wellness builds it in Europe with an ozone system, and the $13,995 price includes White Glove delivery and setup, which on a new-build lot with settling sod is worth having someone else manage. It fills a standard rear yard with room for a walkway.
productBlurbs.the-eden: A lounger for the Bruce Trail hiker who comes home from the Dundas Valley with wrecked calves, in a six-seat European shell with 42 jets, the highest count in the Aquasolus range. The Eden is the lounger version of The Calma at the same $13,995, with White Glove delivery and setup included and an ozone system for simpler water care. Superior Wellness builds it for a market that expects insulation, and it holds heat through a Hamilton February.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-powerpro: Nineteen feet with a hot tub at one end on its own heater, so an Ancaster household with a triathlete and a parent who just wants to soak stops arguing over the thermostat. The J-19DT PowerPro is the strongest swim current Jacuzzi builds, with 53 jets, six seats and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen through quad 50 square foot filters. At $60,895 it is the top of the line, and it needs a big flat lot and a clear path, which is why we site-check first.
productBlurbs.j-19-powerpro: For the swimmer who does not want a hot tub end taking up lane length, the J-19 PowerPro is the full 19 feet of single-temperature swimming with the PowerPro current at $58,995. Four seats and 34 jets are there for recovery after sets, and dual 50 square foot filters with CLEARRAY Active Oxygen handle daily use. It suits a Flamborough acreage where the lot gives the delivery truck a straight run and leaves space for a patio beside it.
productBlurbs.j-16-powerpro: Sixteen feet is the length that fits a Glanbrook subdivision lot and still gives a real swim, which is why the J-16 PowerPro is the swim spa we quote most often. The PowerPro current is the same one you get in the 19 foot model, with four seats and 34 jets for recovery and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen with dual 50 square foot filters. At $54,295 it costs less than a backyard pool and runs in February, when a pool is a tarp.
productBlurbs.j-14-powerpro: Fourteen feet with five seats and 51 jets makes the J-14 PowerPro as much hot tub as swim spa, and it is the PowerPro length that a crane can set into a Westdale yard between the house and the garage. The current is strong enough for a proper workout, the seating is generous enough for a family soak afterward, and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen runs the water care. It is priced at $48,795, and the site check costs nothing.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-poweractive: Swim end and hot tub end on separate heaters, at $53,295 instead of the PowerPro price, is why the J-19DT PowerActive goes to Caledonia country lots along the Grand where there is room for a 19 foot unit. Six seats and 51 jets on the hot side, a PowerActive current on the swim side, four 50 square foot filters and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen. The PowerPro version has a stronger current; most families never miss it.
productBlurbs.j-19-poweractive: A full 19 foot lane at the PowerActive price, $51,395, for a Mount Hope hobby farm with a long driveway and nothing in the way of the delivery. The J-19 PowerActive runs a single water temperature, so it is a swim spa first and a warm soak second, with four seats and 32 jets for the cooldown. CLEARRAY Active Oxygen and dual 50 square foot filters keep the water clear on a well once we set the start-up chemistry.
productBlurbs.j-16-poweractive: Sixteen feet, four seats and 32 jets at $46,495: the J-16 PowerActive is the swim spa for a Brantford family that wants the kids swimming in July and a parent doing laps in January without paying for the PowerPro current. It sits on the same footprint as the J-16 PowerPro, so a standard rear yard on the north end of the city takes it, and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen with dual 50 square foot filters handles Grand River water once we set it up.
productBlurbs.j-14-poweractive: Fourteen feet is the smallest PowerActive, and with five seats and 49 jets it doubles as a large hot tub for a household where two people swim and five people soak. The J-14 PowerActive at $41,395 fits a rear yard no bigger than one parking spot with a path around it, which describes most of the lower city, and it comes in over the house by crane in about an hour. CLEARRAY Active Oxygen and dual filters manage the water.
productBlurbs.j-13-powerplay: Eight seats in 13 feet is the PowerPlay idea: a Fruitland family gets a pool the kids can actually play in, a current strong enough for a parent to swim against, and a soak for eight on a Saturday night, for $33,195. The J-13 PowerPlay runs on a single 32A circuit, uses one 50 square foot DFML filter, and lifts over a rear fence without the road closure a 19 footer sometimes needs. It is the family swim spa we sell most.
productBlurbs.j-12-flow: Twelve feet and $30,695 is the shortest and least expensive swim spa on our floor, and the J-12 Flow is the one that goes onto Ancaster village lots where a longer unit would take the whole yard. Eight seats and 31 jets with CLEARRAY UV-C water care and a 50 square foot DFML filter on a single 32A circuit. The current is meant for aqua exercise and kids more than lap swimming; the J-13 PowerPlay is the step up for a stronger swim.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-dualstream-19: A 19 foot swim lane and a separate five-person hot tub with its own 30 jets and controls, in one shell, at $56,095: the SwimExpert DualStream 19 is what a Millgrove property with room to spare buys instead of a pool and a tub. The swim side has 53 jets and four seats, and ClearStream mineral water care keeps chemical use lower than a chlorine pool, which matters on a well. It is the longest SwimLife unit, so measure the lot before you fall for it.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-aquastream-17: Seventeen feet of swim lane on a 40A circuit with ClearStream mineral water care, priced at $50,095: the SwimExpert AquaStream 17 is for the person who swims for a bad back every morning and wants a current strong enough to be worth it. Three seats and 30 jets give a recovery spot without stealing lane length, and the SwimFit AquaStream 17 is the same length with a lighter spec if the budget is tighter. Stoney Creek Mountain lots take it without a road closure.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-swimstream-14: Fourteen feet on a 32A circuit means the SwimExpert SwimStream 14 goes into a Winona yard without a new panel and without the delivery drama of a longer unit. Three seats, 30 jets and ClearStream mineral water care at $44,795, with the SwimExpert current for someone who swims every day rather than occasionally. Lakeshore wind strips heat off open water, so we position it in the lee of the house and keep the cover on between sessions.
productBlurbs.swimfit-aquastream-17: At $43,795 the SwimFit AquaStream 17 gives you the full 17 foot lane, and a Dundas couple who swim for their knees three mornings a week get everything they need from it: a steady current, three seats, 28 jets and ClearStream mineral water care that is gentle on skin. The SwimExpert AquaStream 17 adds a stronger current for competitive training. On a valley lot we set it on a footed pad so the spring melt does not shift it.
productBlurbs.swimfit-swimstream-14: $38,095 is the lowest priced SwimLife on our floor, and the SwimFit SwimStream 14 spends it on the parts that matter: a 14 foot lane, a 32A circuit that most panels can spare, ClearStream mineral water care and three seats with 28 jets. It goes into a Crown Point yard by crane over the house and gives a winter swimmer a lane when the outdoor pools are closed. Try the current against the SwimExpert SwimStream 14 on our floor.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-1: One person, one standard outlet, and a cabin that fits the spare room of a Corktown apartment: the Sanctuary 1 is the Clearlight for someone who trains alone and wants full spectrum infrared every night without negotiating space. True Wave heaters carry a lifetime warranty along with the cabin, in Basswood or Mahogany, and at $10,495 it includes an AROMA ONE aromatherapy diffuser. The panels come up an apartment stairwell in a couple of trips.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-2: Two people side by side on a household circuit is the most common sauna purchase we make, usually to a couple who both work shifts and want thirty minutes of full spectrum infrared between one schedule and the other. The Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 fits under the low joists of an older basement, comes in Basswood or Mahogany, and the True Wave heaters and cabin carry a lifetime warranty. Our floor unit is heated, so sit in it.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-3: Three seats across a bench is the size a Binbrook family with older kids picks so two people can sit while a third stretches out, and the Sanctuary 3 does it in a cabin that still fits a finished basement room. Full spectrum infrared from True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters, priced at $12,995. It needs a little more room than the Sanctuary 2, so send us your ceiling height before you commit.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-5: The Sanctuary 5 is the largest indoor cabin in the Clearlight range, seating five with the same True Wave full spectrum heaters as the smaller models, at $13,995. It is the cabin we suggest for a heated corner of a Flamborough workshop or a big rec room where a crew of hockey parents or a farm family wants real recovery after a day on concrete. Basswood or Mahogany, lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-y: Four seats at the same price as the five seat Sanctuary 5, with a footprint that fits more basements, which makes the Sanctuary Y the family cabin: an Ancaster household with teenagers in sports gets everyone through a session in one evening. Full spectrum True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany and the lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters come standard at $13,995. It is a larger cabin, so send us your ceiling height and door width before you order.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-c: Four people in a cabin that tucks into a corner is the Sanctuary C, and it is how a Westdale family fits a real sauna into a basement that also holds the laundry and the kids' television. Full spectrum infrared with True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, and the lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters, priced at $14,495. If you have an open wall rather than a corner, the Sanctuary Y gives four seats for a little less.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-retreat: Top of the Clearlight range, four seats with room to stretch, and the one a Grimsby couple who built a wellness room off the garage bought for the whole family. The Sanctuary Retreat runs full spectrum True Wave heaters, comes in Basswood or Mahogany, and carries a lifetime warranty on the cabin and heaters, at $15,295. It is the Clearlight to buy when the sauna is the point of the room and not something squeezed in beside the furnace.
productBlurbs.serenity-mini: Canadian-made from Western red cedar and sized for a smaller yard, the Serenity Mini is the outdoor sauna for a Greensville lot on the escarpment where the flat spot beside the house is the only flat spot. Open bench seating, up to 194 degrees, $14,995 in knotty cedar with clear cedar available, and the heater chosen separately so a wood-burning unit works where a new circuit would not. Set it on footings, because escarpment frost moves gravel.
productBlurbs.serenity-sauna: Built in Canada from Western red cedar, the full-size Serenity Sauna belongs on a Carlisle horse property where the barn has a woodpile and the house panel is already spoken for, because a wood-burning heater needs no circuit at all. Open bench seating, up to 194 degrees, and $17,495 in knotty cedar, with clear cedar and an electric heater as options. Next to the Serenity Mini, it holds a family rather than a couple.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-bath: The Essential Bath is the Chill Tub for someone training for Around the Bay who wants a cold plunge on the patio beside the back door, not a livestock trough and a trip to the gas station for ice. It keeps its own water cold and filtered on a standard outlet, and the bath shape lets you sit rather than stand. Pricing is set at the showroom, and the routine most owners run is sauna, plunge, rest, repeated two or three times.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-pod: Round, upright and small enough for a townhome patio, the Essential Pod is the Chill Tub for a Stoney Creek shift worker who wants a two-minute cold plunge after nights and has no room for a bath-shaped unit. It holds its own water cold and clean on a household outlet, so there is no ice run. Pricing is set at the showroom, and we can quote it alongside a Sanctuary cabin for the full contrast routine.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-obsidian: The Obsidian is the Chill Tub people choose when the plunge sits on a Kirkendall deck they look at from the kitchen and it has to look like it belongs there. It cools and filters on a standard outlet, holds temperature through a humid Hamilton August, and pairs with a Clearlight cabin or a Serenity sauna for heat and cold. Pricing is at the showroom, where it is set up next to the saunas.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-pro: Top of the Chill Tubs range, the Pro is built for the household where cold plunging is daily and shared: a Caledonia firefighter and a partner who runs, both wanting a colder set point and faster recovery between users. It runs its own chiller and filter on a household circuit and sits outside a Serenity or Clearlight door for the walk from heat to cold. Pricing is at the showroom, and it is running on the floor.
productBlurbs.summit-ws190: Ten minutes in the Summit WS190 on our floor tells you more than any spec sheet, which is why we do not publish a price for it; ask at the showroom. It is the top of our two Wellness Shop chairs, and the one a long-haul driver who runs the 403 and Highway 6 all week bought for a back that a hot tub could not reach. Come in after work, sit in it, and compare it with the Dreamcatcher WS170 beside it.
productBlurbs.dreamcatcher-ws170: The Dreamcatcher WS170 is the Wellness Shop chair for someone who sits at a desk all day, at McMaster or in a Hamilton office tower, and wants a full-body massage program in the living room rather than an appointment across town. It is the more compact of our two chairs, and pricing is at the showroom rather than on the site. Both chairs are on the floor, so try each on the same program before deciding.
productBlurbs.duke-series: An enclosed Visscher room with a veranda, built in western red cedar, is what a Binbrook backyard open to the fields needs to make a hot tub usable in a January wind. The Duke Series comes in several sizes, so it fits a six-seat tub with a bench or a seven-seater with a change area, and the enclosed design keeps snow off the cover and the walk to the water short. Pricing and sizing are handled at the showroom.
productBlurbs.cypress-series: Privacy is the reason a Waterdown corner lot with three sets of neighbouring windows ends up with a Cypress Series around the tub. Visscher builds it in western red cedar panels in several sizes, so you can close the sides that face the street and leave the side that faces your own deck open. It weathers the same way a Serenity sauna does, silver on the windward wall. Ask for pricing in the Meadowlands.
productBlurbs.hudson-series: Starting at 11 by 14 feet, the Hudson Series is the enclosed Visscher that swallows an eight-seat J-509 and still leaves room to towel off, which is why it goes to Mount Hope properties with the space for it. Fully enclosed in western red cedar, it turns a tub into a room you use in February without a coat on the walk out. Sizes go up from there, and pricing is at the showroom.
productBlurbs.sequoia-11-14: Louvers you can open on a humid August evening and close against the sun at noon make the Sequoia 11 by 14 the open-air Visscher for a lakeshore yard in Stoney Creek where summer is the season you use the tub most. Western red cedar, 11 by 14 feet, room for a seven-seat tub with a walkway around it, and no walls to trap heat. Pricing is at the showroom, and we can pair it with any tub on the floor.
productBlurbs.sedona-9-9: Nine by nine feet is the footprint for a Nordic round or a J-315 with a little room to stand, and the Sedona 9 by 9 covers that spot in a North End yard without blocking the neighbour's light. Open-air western red cedar, it keeps rain and falling maple keys off the cover and gives the tub a proper place in the yard instead of a corner by the shed. Pricing is done in person.
productBlurbs.savannah-11-11: Square, open and 11 by 11 feet, the Savannah suits a six or seven-seat tub on a new-build lot in Glanbrook where the yard is a rectangle and the tub needs a roof more than walls. Visscher builds it in western red cedar, and the open sides let the summer breeze through while the roof keeps sleet off the cover in a Hamilton winter. Pricing is at the showroom, and it goes up after the tub is set.

financingFaq.q: What does 0% for 12 months OAC actually mean for me?
financingFaq.a: On approved credit, your first twelve months of bi-weekly payments carry no interest at all. After that the balance continues on the amortization set for your product, and longer terms at standard rates are available if you want a lower payment. Your credit file decides approval, and the team can run a second term for you while you are in the showroom.

financingFaq.q: Where does the bi-weekly number on each product come from?
financingFaq.a: It is the advertised starting payment for that model, worked out from today's sale price on the 0% for 12 months offer and subject to credit approval. The amortization varies from product to product, so two tubs with similar prices can show slightly different payments. The full table for every term is in the downloadable price list.

financingFaq.q: Can I roll delivery, a cover lifter or steps into the same payment?
financingFaq.a: Yes. Delivery, covers, lifters, steps, start-up chemicals and any in-store bundle can go into the one financed amount. The electrical hookup is the exception, because your licensed electrician bills that work directly.

financingFaq.q: Will I need a down payment?
financingFaq.a: Usually not on approved credit. If your file calls for one, the team tells you before anything is signed, and you can choose to put money down anyway to shorten the term or lower the bi-weekly figure.

reasons: The 2027 lineup is on its way and the Ancaster floor has to make room for it.
